questions.prompt: How many usable host addresses are in a /24 subnet?
questions.explanation: A /24 has 8 host bits = 256 addresses; subtracting the network and broadcast addresses leaves 254 usable hosts.

questions.prompt: Usable hosts in an IPv4 subnet equals 2 to the power of the host bits, minus ____ (for the network and broadcast addresses).
questions.explanation: You subtract 2 — the network address (all host bits 0) and the broadcast address (all host bits 1) — except in /31 and /32.

questions.prompt: Which statement about CIDR prefixes is correct?

options.text: A larger prefix like /30 means a smaller network with fewer hosts
A larger prefix like /30 means a bigger network with more hosts
The prefix length has no effect on network size

questions.explanation: A larger prefix has more network bits and fewer host bits, so it is a smaller network. /8 is much larger than /24.

questions.prompt: Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: The network address has all host bits set to 0
The broadcast address has all host bits set to 1
Classful Class A/B/C addressing is the current best practice

questions.explanation: Network = host bits 0, broadcast = host bits 1, /31 has both addresses usable (RFC 3021). Classful addressing is obsolete — CIDR replaced it.

questions.prompt: Match each CIDR prefix to its dotted-decimal mask.
Order these subnets from the FEWEST usable hosts to the MOST.
questions.explanation: Smaller prefix numbers mean more host bits and more usable hosts: /30 (2) < /28 (14) < /26 (62) < /24 (254).
